## Mo's own task queue, served over MCP. Agents lease a task, check in while
## working, and report it done or failed. A change to anything compiled in,
## meaning this program, job-queue.mo, lib/ or the compiler's output, refuses the
## saved data of a running queue.
module Main
expose JobFilter(..), Page(..), PageError(..), Stats(..), SubmitError(..)
use JobQueue{Queue, Job, QueueError}

max_payload_bytes = 2048
max_jobs = 5000
max_page_jobs = 100
lease_length = 30.minutes
full_advice = "This limit counts every job ever submitted and never falls, so retrying cannot help. Tell a person."

service
  state Queue = JobQueue.empty
  tools submit, lease, heartbeat, acknowledge, fail, list, stats
  every 1.minute expire
  token from env "QUEUE_TOKEN"
end

enum SubmitError
  PayloadTooLarge(limit: Int, bytes: Int)
  QueueFull(limit: Int, advice: Text)
end

enum JobFilter
  AllJobs
  Ready
  Leased
  Done
  Dead
end

enum PageError
  BadPage(after: Int, limit: Int, max_limit: Int)
end

struct Page
  jobs: List(Job)
  next: Option(Int)
  now: Time
end

struct Stats
  total: Int
  ready: Int
  leased: Int
  done: Int
  dead: Int
  limit: Int
  now: Time
end

## Adds a task and returns its id. Every Int in this service, in arguments and
## replies, is a JSON string.
## `payload` is free text handed to a worker unchanged, at most 2,048 bytes. Give
## a short brief and say where the rest is. It is kept for good and any token
## holder can read it, so keep secrets out.
## PayloadTooLarge gives the limit and the size sent: shorten it. HTTP 413 means
## the request body passed 16 KiB, so the payload never reached the queue:
## shorten it.
## QueueFull: the limit of 5,000 counts every job ever submitted, including Done
## and Dead, and never falls. Retrying cannot help, so tell a person.
## Not safe to retry blindly: a retry after a lost reply or store_failed makes a
## second job, so check `list` first.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit. Five
## of those in 60 seconds restart the service, and three restarts stop it for
## everyone until a person starts it.
fn submit(queue: Queue, _now: Time, payload: Text) : Result((Queue, Int), SubmitError)
  bytes = payload.byte_count
  return Error(PayloadTooLarge(limit: max_payload_bytes, bytes: bytes)) if bytes > max_payload_bytes
  return Error(QueueFull(limit: max_jobs, advice: full_advice)) if JobQueue.jobs(queue).size >=
    max_jobs
  Ok(JobQueue.submit(queue, payload))
end

## Leases the oldest ready task for 30 minutes and counts an attempt. Replies
## {"case":"None"} when nothing is ready, and nothing will notify you. To look
## without taking anything, use `list`. Wait a minute before calling this again.
## {"case":"Some","value":job} gives you the job. A job is {"id","payload",
## "attempts","state"}, and `state` is {"case":"Ready"}, {"case":"Leased","fields":
## {"until":time}}, {"case":"Done"} or {"case":"Dead"}. Pass `job.id` as `id` and
## `job.attempts` as `attempt` to the other tools, and keep both somewhere that
## survives losing your context: no tool tells you which job is yours. The lease ends at
## `job.state.fields.until`. Call `heartbeat` about every 10 minutes.
## If `job.attempts` is above 1, an earlier attempt ran and may have left partial
## work, so check before starting. The third attempt that fails or expires makes
## the job Dead for good; a coordinator re-submits it as a new job or tells a
## person.
## Never hold a lease while waiting on a person, such as for a PR review: the
## lease runs out and another worker repeats the task. Acknowledge at hand-off.
## Not safe to retry: after a lost reply the job stays held by nobody until the
## lease ends, and one attempt is spent.
## A tool's own refusal is {"error":{"kind":"application","value":{"case":...}}}.
## A runtime error is {"error":{"kind":"runtime","code":...,"message":...,
## "effect":...}}, where `effect` says what this call did to the queue: none,
## applied or unknown. It does not say whether a retry is safe.
## What to do about runtime errors, on every tool:
## - busy, rate_limited: wait, then retry.
## - invalid_arguments: fix the call; do not repeat it.
## - handler_failed, work_limit, memory_limit: never repeat the call, and tell a
##   person. Five of those in 60 seconds restart the service, and three restarts
##   stop it for everyone until a person starts it. With effect none, your lease
##   still ends when it did, so keep working inside it.
## - store_failed, or no reply at all: the outcome is unknown, so treat it as a
##   lost reply for that tool.
## - stopped: the service is down until a person starts it. Stop calling and keep
##   your id and attempt.
## - response_limit: on `list`, lower `limit`. On a tool that changes the queue,
##   the change was applied.
fn lease(queue: Queue, now: Time) : Result((Queue, Option(Job)), QueueError)
  JobQueue.lease(queue, now, lease_length)
end

## Renews your lease for 30 minutes from now without counting an attempt. Call it
## about every 10 minutes while working, and before any step that may block for
## over 20 minutes. `id` is `job.id` and `attempt` is `job.attempts`, both JSON
## strings from `lease`. Safe to retry.
## NotLeased: read the job with `list`, using filter {"case":"AllJobs"}, `after`
## id - 1 and `limit` 1, then compare. Done with your attempt: your acknowledge
## landed, so that is success. Ready or Leased with your attempt: your lease ran
## out, so stop. Dead: stop and report. More attempts than yours: a later attempt
## owns the job, so stop.
## NoSuchJob: the id is wrong; do not retry.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit: it
## can stop the service for everyone.
fn heartbeat(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result((Queue, Unit), QueueError)
  after = try JobQueue.heartbeat(queue, now, id, attempt)
  Ok((after, Unit))
end

## Marks your leased job Done. A task ends at hand-off: acknowledge when your PR
## opens or your work is delivered, not after a person reviews it. `id` is
## `job.id` and `attempt` is `job.attempts`, both JSON strings from `lease`. Safe
## to retry.
## NotLeased does not mean your work failed: read the job with `list`, using
## filter {"case":"AllJobs"}, `after` id - 1 and `limit` 1, then compare. Done
## with your attempt: your earlier acknowledge landed, so that is success. Ready
## or Leased with your attempt: your lease ran out, so stop and tell the
## coordinator what you delivered. Dead: stop and report. More attempts than
## yours: a later attempt owns the job, so stop and do not acknowledge.
## NoSuchJob: the id is wrong; do not retry.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit: it
## can stop the service for everyone.
fn acknowledge(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result((Queue, Unit), QueueError)
  after = try JobQueue.acknowledge(queue, now, id, attempt)
  Ok((after, Unit))
end

## Gives your leased job back when you cannot finish it. It goes back to Ready,
## or to Dead on its third attempt, and a Dead job is never retried. The queue
## may hand the same job to the next `lease`. `id` is `job.id` and `attempt` is
## `job.attempts`, both JSON strings from `lease`. Safe to retry.
## NotLeased: read the job with `list`, using filter {"case":"AllJobs"}, `after`
## id - 1 and `limit` 1, then compare. Done with your attempt: an earlier
## acknowledge landed. Ready or Leased with your attempt: your lease ran out or
## your earlier fail landed, so stop. Dead: stop and report. More attempts than

## NoSuchJob: the id is wrong; do not retry.

## The core of a job queue. Jobs are submitted, leased to a worker for a while,
## and acknowledged when done. A lease that fails or expires puts its job back
## in the queue, up to three attempts in all; after the third, the job is dead.
## The queue is a value: every operation returns the new queue, and no
## operation ever loses a job.
module JobQueue
expose Queue,
Job(..),
JobState(..),
QueueError(..),
empty,
submit,
lease,
heartbeat,
acknowledge,
fail,
expire,
jobs

max_attempts = 3

struct Job
  id: Int
  payload: Text
  attempts: Int
  state: JobState
end

enum JobState
  Ready
  Leased(until: Time)
  Done
  Dead
end

struct Queue
  jobs: Map(Int, Job)
  next_id: Int
end

enum QueueError
  NoSuchJob(id: Int)
  NotLeased(id: Int)
  BadLease(length: Duration)
end

empty = Queue(jobs: {}, next_id: 1)

fn submit(queue: Queue, payload: Text) : (Queue, Int)
  promise "a submitted job is in the queue, ready"
    result.0.jobs.get(result.1) is Some(job) and job.state == Ready
    allows queue: empty, payload: "x", result: (holding([ready(1)]), 1)
    forbids queue: empty, payload: "x", result: (empty, 1)
  end

  id = queue.next_id
  var after = queue
  after.jobs = after.jobs.set(id, Job(id: id, payload: payload, attempts: 0, state: Ready))
  after.next_id += 1
  (after, id)
end

## Leases the oldest ready job until now + length, counting an attempt. The
## length must be positive, and the lease must end by the year 9999.
fn lease(queue: Queue, now: Time, length: Duration) : Result((Queue, Option(Job)), QueueError)
  promise "a lease never loses a job"
    result is Ok((after, _)) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(id) after.jobs.has?(id) end)
    allows queue: holding([ready(1)]), now: t0, length: 30.seconds, result: Ok((
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]),
      Some(leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds))
    ))
    forbids queue: holding([ready(1)]), now: t0, length: 30.seconds, result: Ok((empty, None))
  end

  examples
    lease(empty, t0, 30.seconds) == Ok((empty, None))
    lease(empty, t0, 0.seconds) == Error(BadLease(length: 0.seconds))
  end

  return Error(BadLease(length: length)) if length <= 0.seconds
  until = try now.checked_add(length).or_fail(BadLease(length: length))
  case queue.jobs.values.find(fn(job) job.state == Ready end)
    None: Ok((queue, None))
    Some(job):
      var taken = job
      taken.state = Leased(until: until)
      taken.attempts += 1
      Ok((put(queue, taken), Some(taken)))
  end
end

## Renews the current lease until now + 30 minutes without counting an attempt.
## NotLeased also covers an expired lease or a different attempt.
fn heartbeat(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can be renewed"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])
    )
  end

  promise "renewing a lease keeps every job and its attempt"
    result is Ok(after) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(other) after.jobs.has?(other) end)
    result is Ok(after) implies
      after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        now.checked_add(30.minutes) == Some(until)
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes), ready(2)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])
    )
  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  until = try now.checked_add(30.minutes).or_fail(BadLease(length: 30.minutes))
  var renewed = job
  renewed.state = Leased(until: until)
  Ok(put(queue, renewed))
end

## Finishes a current lease. Expired or mismatched attempts return NotLeased.
fn acknowledge(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can be acknowledged"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
  end

  promise "acknowledging finishes the job and keeps every job"
    result is Ok(after) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(other) after.jobs.has?(other) end)
    result is Ok(after) implies after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and job.state == Done
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1), ready(2)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  var finished = job
  finished.state = Done
  Ok(put(queue, finished))
end

## Gives a current lease back after its worker failed: ready again, or dead after
## its last attempt. Expired or mismatched attempts return NotLeased.
fn fail(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can fail"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([tried(1, 2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([retried(1, 2)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([tried(1, 2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([retried(1, 2)])
    )
  end

  promise "a job is attempted at most three times"
    result is Ok(after) and after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and job.attempts >= max_attempts implies
      job.state == Dead
    allows queue: holding([tried(1, 3)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 3, result: Ok(holding([dead(1)]))
    forbids queue: holding([tried(1, 3)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 3, result: Ok(
      holding([retried(1, 3)])
    )
  end

  examples
    fail(holding([tried(1, 1)]), t0, 1, 1) == Ok(holding([retried(1, 1)]))
    fail(holding([tried(1, 3)]), t0, 1, 3) == Ok(holding([dead(1)]))
    fail(holding([ready(1)]), t0, 1, 0) == Error(NotLeased(id: 1))
    fail(empty, t0, 9, 1) == Error(NoSuchJob(id: 9))
  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  Ok(release(queue, job))
end

## Gives back every job whose lease ran out by now, as if its worker failed.
fn expire(queue: Queue, now: Time) : Queue
  examples
    expire(holding([leased(1, t0)]), t0) == holding([retried(1, 1)])
    expire(holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), t0) == holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)])
  end

  var after = queue
  for job in queue.jobs.values
    if job.state is Leased(until: until) and until <= now
      after = release(after, job)
    end
  end
  after
end

## Every job in the queue, in id order, whatever its state.
fn jobs(queue: Queue) : List(Job)
  examples
    jobs(empty) == []
    jobs(holding([ready(1), done(2)])) == [ready(1), done(2)]
    fail(holding([tried(1, 1), ready(2)]), t0, 1, 1).map(jobs) == Ok([retried(1, 1), ready(2)])
  end

  queue.jobs.values
end

fn leased_job(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Job, QueueError)
  job = try queue.jobs.get(id).or_fail(NoSuchJob(id: id))
  case job.state
    Leased(until: until): if job.attempts == attempt and until > now: Ok(job) else: Error(
      NotLeased(id: id)
    )
    Ready | Done | Dead: Error(NotLeased(id: id))
  end
end

fn release(queue: Queue, job: Job) : Queue
  var released = job
  released.state = if job.attempts >= max_attempts: Dead else: Ready
  put(queue, released)
end

fn put(queue: Queue, job: Job) : Queue
  var after = queue
  after.jobs = after.jobs.set(job.id, job)
  after
end

## The core of a job queue. Jobs are submitted, leased to a worker for a while,
## and acknowledged when done. A lease that fails or expires puts its job back
## in the queue, up to three attempts in all; after the third, the job is dead.
## The queue is a value: every operation returns the new queue, and no
## operation ever loses a job.
module JobQueue
expose Queue,
Job(..),
JobState(..),
QueueError(..),
empty,
submit,
lease,
heartbeat,
acknowledge,
fail,
expire,
jobs

max_attempts = 3

struct Job
  id: Int
  payload: Text
  attempts: Int
  state: JobState
end

enum JobState
  Ready
  Leased(until: Time)
  Done
  Dead
end

struct Queue
  jobs: Map(Int, Job)
  next_id: Int
end

enum QueueError
  NoSuchJob(id: Int)
  NotLeased(id: Int)
  BadLease(length: Duration)
end

empty = Queue(jobs: {}, next_id: 1)

fn submit(queue: Queue, payload: Text) : (Queue, Int)
  promise "a submitted job is in the queue, ready"
    result.0.jobs.get(result.1) is Some(job) and job.state == Ready
    allows queue: empty, payload: "x", result: (holding([ready(1)]), 1)
    forbids queue: empty, payload: "x", result: (empty, 1)
  end

  id = queue.next_id
  var after = queue
  after.jobs = after.jobs.set(id, Job(id: id, payload: payload, attempts: 0, state: Ready))
  after.next_id += 1
  (after, id)
end

## Leases the oldest ready job until now + length, counting an attempt. The
## length must be positive, and the lease must end by the year 9999.
fn lease(queue: Queue, now: Time, length: Duration) : Result((Queue, Option(Job)), QueueError)
  promise "a lease never loses a job"
    result is Ok((after, _)) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(id) after.jobs.has?(id) end)
    allows queue: holding([ready(1)]), now: t0, length: 30.seconds, result: Ok((
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]),
      Some(leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds))
    ))
    forbids queue: holding([ready(1)]), now: t0, length: 30.seconds, result: Ok((empty, None))
  end

  examples
    lease(empty, t0, 30.seconds) == Ok((empty, None))
    lease(empty, t0, 0.seconds) == Error(BadLease(length: 0.seconds))
  end

  return Error(BadLease(length: length)) if length <= 0.seconds
  until = try now.checked_add(length).or_fail(BadLease(length: length))
  case queue.jobs.values.find(fn(job) job.state == Ready end)
    None: Ok((queue, None))
    Some(job):
      var taken = job
      taken.state = Leased(until: until)
      taken.attempts += 1
      Ok((put(queue, taken), Some(taken)))
  end
end

## Renews the current lease until now + 30 minutes without counting an attempt.
## NotLeased also covers an expired lease or a different attempt.
fn heartbeat(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can be renewed"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])
    )
  end

  promise "renewing a lease keeps every job and its attempt"
    result is Ok(after) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(other) after.jobs.has?(other) end)
    result is Ok(after) implies
      after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        now.checked_add(30.minutes) == Some(until)
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes), ready(2)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])
    )
  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  until = try now.checked_add(30.minutes).or_fail(BadLease(length: 30.minutes))
  var renewed = job
  renewed.state = Leased(until: until)
  Ok(put(queue, renewed))
end

## Finishes a current lease. Expired or mismatched attempts return NotLeased.
fn acknowledge(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can be acknowledged"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
  end

  promise "acknowledging finishes the job and keeps every job"
    result is Ok(after) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(other) after.jobs.has?(other) end)
    result is Ok(after) implies after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and job.state == Done
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1), ready(2)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  var finished = job
  finished.state = Done
  Ok(put(queue, finished))
end

## Gives a current lease back after its worker failed: ready again, or dead after
## its last attempt. Expired or mismatched attempts return NotLeased.
fn fail(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can fail"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and

A promise whose inputs include a `Simulation` is E1400; promises over a service's sequences of steps are deferred. `mo run` on a service entry module still refuses with E1408, "mo run does not start services yet". `mo test` runs one recovery check for each service in the program, named after its module, such as `Counter.service.recovery` (reference 12.5). Its author writes nothing for it. It shares a promise's budget: `--seconds` bounds its time and `--calls` caps its sequences. For `counter.mo` under Run a service, `mo test counter.mo` prints `passed Counter.service.recovery  counter.mo:3:1`, then `1 passed, 0 failed, 0 stopped`. A failing check prints the numbered steps of a shrunk sequence, with literal arguments and each step's outcome, then the state before the crash and the state recovery produced. When the deadline ends before the check compares a restart, `mo test` reports E1404, "the deadline ended before the check compared a restart".
